Marathon Petroleum stock rose modestly today as oil refining conditions remained favorable for the company's core business. US crude is trading at $97.26 per barrel while refineries are running at 97.8% capacity—near maximum utilization—which typically means strong margins for refiners who convert crude into gasoline and diesel. The stock has climbed 8.91% over the past two weeks as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and threats to shipping lanes, have kept crude prices elevated and supported energy sector valuations.

The broader backdrop is sustained uncertainty in global oil markets: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shutdown, Houthi advances toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (a critical chokepoint for oil shipments), and the Iran conflict have all pushed prices higher this week despite a modest pullback on Friday. For a refiner, higher crude prices can cut into profits if retail fuel prices don't keep pace, but the current environment of tight global supply and high refining utilization rates has generally supported the sector.
